audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Ephesian disciples, holy Spirit, Tyrannus hall, unusual powers, sons of Sceva, costly scrolls, Artemis riot.

verses.restored: It happened while Apollos was in Corinth that Paul, passing through the upper regions, came to Ephesus and found some disciples.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,

verses.restored: He said to them, Did you receive holy Spirit when you trusted? They said to him, But we have not even heard whether there is holy Spirit.

familiar.text: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.

verses.restored: He said, Into what then were you baptized? They said, Into John's baptism.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism.

verses.restored: Paul said, John baptized a baptism of turning/realignment, saying to the people that they should trust into the one coming after him, that is, into Jesus.

familiar.text: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.

verses.restored: Hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

familiar.text: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.restored: When Paul had laid hands on them, the holy Spirit came upon them, and they were speaking in tongues and prophesying.

familiar.text: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.

verses.restored: There were about twelve men in all.

familiar.text: And all the men were about twelve.

verses.restored: Entering the synagogue, he spoke boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading concerning the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.

verses.restored: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking harmfully of the Way before the multitude, he withdrew from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.

familiar.text: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.

verses.restored: This happened for two years, so that all those dwelling in Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Judeans and Greeks.

familiar.text: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.

verses.restored: The Divine was doing extraordinary powers through the hands of Paul,

familiar.text: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:

verses.restored: so that even cloths or aprons from his skin were carried away to the weak, and the diseases left them, and harmful spirits went out.

familiar.text: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.

verses.restored: Some of the traveling Judean exorcists attempted to name over those having harmful spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul proclaims.

familiar.text: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the LORD Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.

verses.restored: There were seven sons of a certain Sceva, a Judean chief priest, doing this.

familiar.text: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.

verses.restored: The harmful spirit answered and said to them, Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize; but you, who are you?

familiar.text: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?

verses.restored: The human in whom the harmful spirit was leaped upon them, mastered them all, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

familiar.text: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

verses.restored: This became known to all Judeans and Greeks dwelling in Ephesus, and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

familiar.text: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

verses.restored: Many of those who had trusted were coming, confessing and reporting their practices.

familiar.text: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.

verses.restored: Many of those who practiced magic arts brought together the scrolls and burned them before all; they counted their prices and found fifty thousand pieces of silver.

familiar.text: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.

verses.restored: Thus by the Lord's power the word was growing and prevailing.

familiar.text: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.

verses.restored: When these things were fulfilled, Paul set in the Spirit to pass through Macedonia and Achaia and go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, it is necessary for me also to see Rome.

familiar.text: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.

verses.restored: Sending into Macedonia two of those serving him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed for a time in Asia.

familiar.text: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.

verses.restored: About that time there happened no small disturbance concerning the Way.

familiar.text: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.

verses.restored: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith making silver shrines of Artemis, provided no little business to the craftsmen.

familiar.text: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;

verses.restored: Gathering them and the workers of such things, he said, Men, you know that from this business comes our prosperity.

familiar.text: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.

verses.restored: You see and hear that not only in Ephesus but almost in all Asia this Paul has persuaded and turned away a considerable crowd, saying that those made by hands are not gods.

familiar.text: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:

verses.restored: Not only is there danger that this trade of ours may come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis be counted as nothing, and that she be about to be pulled down from her magnificence, whom all Asia and the inhabited world revere.

familiar.text: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.

verses.restored: Hearing this and becoming full of rage, they cried out, saying, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians.

familiar.text: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

verses.restored: The city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, seizing Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, Paul's travel companions.

familiar.text: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.

verses.restored: Paul wanted to go in to the people, but the disciples would not let him.

familiar.text: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.

verses.restored: Some of the Asiarchs also, being friendly to him, sent to him and urged him not to give himself into the theater.

familiar.text: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.

verses.restored: Therefore some cried one thing, some another, for the assembly was confused, and most did not know why they had come together.

familiar.text: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.

verses.restored: Some from the crowd instructed Alexander, the Judeans pushing him forward. Alexander motioned with his hand and wanted to make a defense to the people.

familiar.text: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.

verses.restored: But recognizing that he was Judean, one voice came from all, crying for about two hours, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians.

familiar.text: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

verses.restored: The city clerk quieted the crowd and said, Men of Ephesus, who among humans does not know that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great Artemis and of the heaven-fallen image?

familiar.text: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?

verses.restored: Since these things cannot be denied, it is necessary for you to be quiet and do nothing reckless.

familiar.text: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.

verses.restored: For you brought these men who are neither temple-robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.

familiar.text: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.

verses.restored: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a matter against anyone, courts are held and there are proconsuls; let them accuse one another.

familiar.text: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.

verses.restored: But if you seek anything further, it will be resolved in the lawful assembly.

familiar.text: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.

verses.restored: For indeed we are in danger of being accused of riot concerning today, since there is no cause by which we will be able to give account for this disorderly gathering.

familiar.text: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.

verses.restored: Saying these things, he dismissed the assembly.

familiar.text: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
